author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The northern store incident proves that manual checks are not a safety net, they are a single point of failure. When a batch of till scan lines drops silently, the model forecasts zero demand for fresh produce, and the damage is done before anyone notices. I need the entire ingestion pipeline to run on its own, with no human handoff between the till feeds and the feature store. Every store must deliver its data on time, automatically, every night. The more automated the flow, the faster we can catch a gap before it becomes a shelf gap. I am asking for full automation because partial automation just moves the risk to a different hour. I want the system to guarantee arrival without anyone needing to remember to check.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that they want the system to guarantee arrival without human intervention and argues that more automation leads to faster detection of gaps, indicating that exceeding the minimum ask (full automation) would make them happier.
